title: Asset and Protocol
premise: Freya Yarrow, a financial-crimes investigator who specializes in cases powerful people want buried, notices that a private flight's records have been erased while the plane is still airborne—a digital vanishing act only someone inside the system could perform. Following the money, she uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' over Frankfurt timed to crash markets before opening bell, orchestrated by the very institution that trained her and protected by her late father's old network. Torn between loyalty to her mentor Marcus Hale—who may be either her ally or the architect—and her growing bond with whistleblower pilot Tomas Reiner, Freya must decide whether exposing the truth will save lives or destroy everything her family built. In the end she stops the attack minutes before Frankfurt opens, but at the cost of burning her own inheritance: she publishes the evidence implicating her father's legacy and walks away from the invisible life that once kept her safe.
about_author: Isandro Voss is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about systems—how they protect people, and how they fail them.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Freya Yarrow closes another unattributable case for the Directorate, scrubbing a shipping magnate's ledger until it gleams. POV Freya. Beat: competent numbness—the reader sees how much of herself she has traded for invisibility.

chapters.title: The Unattributed File
chapters.summary: Her supervisor hands her a file with no case number: a mid-air transponder anomaly over the North Sea. POV Freya. Beat: first itch of curiosity; something in the paperwork feels wrong in a way she can't name.

chapters.title: Gone While Airborne
chapters.summary: Freya confirms the impossible: flight records deleted while the aircraft was still transmitting. She pulls raw radar archives against orders. POV Freya. Beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Hale's Warning
chapters.summary: Mentor Marcus Hale gently suggests she drop it, invoking her father's memory. POV Freya. Beat: warmth laced with threat; loyalty begins to feel like a leash.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: She tracks down the flight's co-pilot, Tomas Reiner, who survived a 'mechanical' grounding and suspects he was meant to be aboard. POV Tomas. Beat: wary connection between two people who trust nothing.

chapters.title: Shell Game
chapters.summary: Following insurance premiums, Freya finds a chain of shells registered to a foundation bearing her father's name. POV Freya. Beat: personal violation—the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Tomas shows her a smuggled maintenance log proving the aircraft was sabotaged, not malfunctioning. POV Tomas. Beat: fear becoming resolve; they agree to work together.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Freya maps the financial positions betting against European aviation futures—all expiring the morning of a scheduled Frankfurt session. POV Freya. Beat: cold clarity; this isn't history, it's rehearsal.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: She discovers the deletion tool used on the flight data is an internal Directorate program called LACUNA. POV Freya. Beat: betrayal—the institution itself is the weapon.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Rotterdam
chapters.summary: A contact who promised evidence is found drowned; his dead drop contains half a hard drive. POV Freya. Beat: grief and guilt; the case now has a body count.

chapters.title: What Father Built
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Freya learns her father laundered money for causes he called necessary. POV Freya (past). Beat: understanding without forgiveness; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: The Second Flight
chapters.summary: Pattern analysis reveals a second aircraft booked under a charity's name, routed toward Frankfurt. POV Freya. Beat: urgency—the 'accident' has a date.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Someone follows Freya home; she loses them but knows she's been catalogued. POV Freya. Beat: paranoia; invisibility is failing.

chapters.title: Hale's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Marcus admits LACUNA exists and claims he's trying to contain it from within. POV Hale. Beat: ambiguous sympathy—is he protector or handler?

chapters.title: The Charity Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas infiltrates the charity's office and photographs donor records linking to a Frankfurt clearing house. POV Tomas. Beat: courage rewarded, then nearly fatal—he's spotted.

chapters.title: Safe House
chapters.summary: Wounded and hunted, Tomas hides with Freya; between bandages and bad coffee, something tender takes root. POV alternating. Beat: love against duty, chosen explicitly.

chapters.title: LACUNA's Author
chapters.summary: Code forensics show LACUNA was written by her father's team twenty years ago—and updated last month. POV Freya. Beat: horror; the ghost is active.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Freya attends a Directorate briefing where the second flight is dismissed as routine. She says nothing. POV Freya. Beat: complicity; silence as a moral choice.

chapters.title: Reiner's Record
chapters.summary: Tomas's flight logs are wiped remotely; his apartment burns that night. POV Tomas. Beat: loss of everything except each other and the truth.

chapters.title: Half a Drive
chapters.summary: Freya decrypts the Rotterdam drive fragment: a manifest naming the target—a trading floor beneath the flight path. POV Freya. Beat: the scale lands; not markets, people.

chapters.title: Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: An anonymous message offers Freya her father's full archive in exchange for walking away. POV Freya. Beat: temptation made flesh; the price is Tomas's safety.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to No One
chapters.summary: Introduction of Voss-adjacent antagonist 'Counselor Brandt,' the fixer who maintains the invisible world. POV Brandt. Beat: elegant menace; he genuinely believes he prevents wars.

chapters.title: Trust Exercise
chapters.summary: Freya tests Hale by feeding him false information; it reaches Brandt within hours. POV Freya. Beat: heartbreak—her mentor is compromised, willingly or not.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: She reconstructs the planned route: the aircraft will 'lose' transponder over dense morning traffic near Frankfurt. POV Freya. Beat: countdown pressure; hours matter now.

chapters.title: The Archive Offer
chapters.summary: Freya meets Brandt's courier, takes the archive, and immediately copies it three ways. POV Freya. Beat: playing both sides; her father's lessons finally useful.

chapters.title: Father's Voice
chapters.summary: The archive includes a video: her father explaining LACUNA was built to erase one flight—a witness transport—and it never stopped running. POV Freya (archive). Beat: the inheritance revealed as machinery of erasure.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Authorities revoke Tomas's license on fabricated grounds, stranding him as a witness no court will hear. POV Tomas. Beat: despair; the system closes every legal door.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Freya calculates the attack window: dawn, before Frankfurt opens. She has one day. POV Freya. Beat: ticking clock formalized; plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: She approaches a disgraced air-traffic controller and a journalist who owes her, assembling a crew of the discarded. POV Freya. Beat: hope through unlikely fellowship.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Confronted with proof, Hale breaks: he'll give her the ground-station override codes if she promises to expose him too. POV Hale. Beat: redemption priced honestly; duty inverted into truth.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Preparations: jamming contingencies, press embargo drafts, Tomas volunteering to fly intercept. POV alternating. Beat: quiet before catastrophe; love stated plainly, maybe for the last time.

chapters.title: Lift-Off
chapters.summary: The target aircraft departs early. The clock starts for real. POV Freya. Beat: adrenaline; no more analysis, only action.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Brandt's people cut Freya's communications; she drives toward the control center through pre-dawn fog. POV Freya. Beat: isolation at maximum velocity.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Tomas, flying a chartered trainer, reaches the aircraft and transmits the sabotage evidence directly to its cockpit, forcing the pilots to divert rather than complete the run. POV Tomas. Beat: bravery as persuasion; the human argument beats the protocol.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: The diverted plane lands; Frankfurt opens on an ordinary morning. Markets barely notice what didn't happen. POV Freya. Beat: anticlimax as triumph—the best outcome is a non-event.

chapters.title: Brandt's Fall
chapters.summary: Freya releases the full archive—her father included—to the journalist. Brandt is arrested quietly; the system eats its own. POV Freya. Beat: justice without satisfaction.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya testifies publicly, ending her own unattributability. Hale, true to the deal, corroborates and accepts charges. POV Freya. Beat: grief and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Tomas and Freya sort through her father's effects, keeping almost nothing. POV alternating. Beat: mourning the myth of the father; choosing each other.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Epilogue-style scene: months later, Freya's name appears on a published report—the first case ever attributed to her. POV Freya. Beat: visibility embraced; the invisible woman signs her work.

chapters.title: Asset and Protocol
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a new anomaly pings an old inbox—but this time Freya reads it in daylight, with Tomas beside her, deciding together whether to answer. POV Freya. Beat: open horizon; duty redefined as shared choice rather than inherited silence.
